question: Are the attention-head representations that causally mediate in-context learning also invariant representations of the underlying relational concept across question formats and languages?

key_findings.claim: Author method: Function Vectors and Concept Vectors use the same additive head-output construction but select heads with different objectives—causal indirect effect versus format-invariant representational similarity.
key_findings.evidence: Activation patching ranks heads by the probability gain for the expected answer when a clean mean activation is transplanted into a corrupted prompt. RSA instead correlates each head's prompt-pair cosine-similarity matrix with a binary same-concept design matrix that ignores format. The top-K AIE or RSA heads are summed to form FVs or CVs, respectively.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported representation result: RSA-selected CVs organize more by concept and less by question type than AIE-selected FVs across the four tested models.
key_findings.evidence: Across seven relations, three formats, and multiple K values, Figure 4 reports higher concept RSA and lower question-type RSA for CVs. In Llama-3.1-70B, FV similarities have a strong within-format cluster with mean cosine 0.90, whereas CVs cluster more by relation across formats but retain a weaker format cluster with mean cosine 0.55. Appendix B shows analogous matrices for the other models.

anchors.section: Appendix B similarity matrices for other models

key_findings.claim: Author-reported localization result: CV and FV heads occupy similar layer ranges but their top-ranked identities are almost disjoint.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports zero overlap for every model at K=3 and K=5, and zero or one overlap at K=10; even at K=100 the intersections are 28/6/39/13 for Llama-8B/Llama-70B/Qwen-7B/Qwen-72B. Layer-averaged RSA and AIE profiles peak in broadly similar regions, while the AIE histogram is highly sparse. The hypergeometric test only finds above-chance overlap in some larger-K cells.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported steering trade-off: FVs give larger in-format gains, while CVs usually retain positive, concept-aligned effects more consistently when extracted from French or multiple-choice prompts.
key_findings.evidence: Vectors are added to the last-token residual stream in AmbiguousICL, where a first relation competes with a later English-to-French translation relation. Across the displayed models and relations, English open-ended FVs usually produce the largest target-probability gains. OOD FVs often weaken or emit extraction-format artifacts, whereas CV curves are generally smaller but more similar across extraction formats.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported token analysis: OOD FVs visibly mix the intended relation with language or response-format signals, while CV outputs remain more concept-aligned in the showcased example.
key_findings.evidence: For the query 'salty', the unsteered Llama-3.1-70B assigns 49% to the French translation and 2% to 'sweet'. The English FV raises 'sweet' by 56 points, but its French FV raises French subwords and its MC FV raises the opening bracket by 53 points. All three CVs instead rank English antonyms highest, raising 'sweet' by 49, 54, and 35 points. Spanish-extracted FVs also raise French translations, suggesting a generic foreign-language rather than French-specific signal.

anchors.section: 3.2.3 Function Vectors Mix Concept with Input Format
Appendix G language and bracket effects

key_findings.claim: Author-reported consistency metric: post-steering next-token distributions are closer between ID and OOD extraction formats for CVs than for FVs.
key_findings.evidence: For each relation and vector type, the authors select the five layers with highest ID target-probability gain and average KL[p(.|v_OOD) || p(.|v_ID)] across prompts and layers. Figure 8 reports lower CV KL in every model summary, with a larger CV-FV gap for multiple-choice than French extraction; the Spanish-context replication in Llama-3.1-70B has the same ordering.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: lower CV KL does not by itself establish better directional generalization because it is confounded by intervention strength.
key_findings.evidence: The paper repeatedly reports that CVs have smaller absolute gains and minimal zero-shot effect. Two weak perturbations naturally remain closer to each other and to the unsteered distribution than two strong perturbations. The KL comparison does not magnitude-match ID effects, normalize divergence by target-probability change, or compare equal-norm/equal-effect interventions. Token-level and positive-gain evidence supports some transfer, but the KL magnitude cannot be assigned wholly to abstraction.

anchors.section: Implications for steering and zero-shot limitation

key_findings.claim: Negative result: CVs are largely ineffective at instantiating a missing task from scratch and are not recovered by the activation-patching causal localizer.
key_findings.evidence: Zero-shot plots show little CV steering compared with FVs, and the discussion says CVs appear to require the relation already in the prompt. Cross-format patching across all six format directions finds 1-4 overlapping top-5 FV heads but zero CV heads in every direction. The authors therefore position CVs as modulators of an existing abstract signal rather than substitutes for FVs.

anchors.section: Appendix O cross-format activation patching, Table 4

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the claimed OOD steering generalization is not a strictly held-out OOD evaluation because French and multiple-choice effects are used to choose the steering hyperparameters.
key_findings.evidence: The main text calls OE-FR and MC out of distribution relative to AmbiguousICL and reports the best alpha and K per model. Appendix F states that alpha and K are optimized on antonym prompts by maximizing average steering effect across all input formats—that is, the ID and both designated OOD formats. The same tuned formats and the antonym relation are then included in the reported generalization results, so this is cross-format transfer after format-aware tuning, not untouched OOD model selection.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the cross-format patching evidence is narrower than the conclusion that the same FV heads are the primary causal mechanism regardless of format.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix O is reported only for Llama-3.1-70B. Its top-5 overlap with standard FVs varies from four heads to one, and maximum AIE falls to 0.02 for OE-EN to MC and 0.01 for OE-FR to MC. The experiment supports some recurring FV heads and no top-5 CV recovery in this model, but tiny effects and one-head overlap in some directions do not establish a format-independent primary mechanism across all four models.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: the central representational comparison is selection-conditioned and partly in-sample.
key_findings.evidence: CV heads are defined by maximizing same-concept RSA across the 21 concept-format datasets, then their superior concept RSA and similarity clustering are evaluated on those same formats and prompt collection. This validates that the selector works but cannot alone show generalization to unseen relations or surface forms. The distinct AmbiguousICL prompts, Spanish context, and steering effects add evidence, yet the seven word-level relations and two model families remain a narrow abstraction test.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: context-sensitive steering is compatible with an abstract modulator, but does not demonstrate the paper's stronger claim that CVs are symbolic pointers to content stored elsewhere.
key_findings.evidence: English-extracted CVs can favor a Spanish antonym when Spanish context already specifies the surface realization, while CVs fail zero-shot. This is evidence for context dependence and relation modulation. No content-addressing circuit, pointer target, read/write pathway, or mediation from CV heads to an independently localized content store is identified, so 'pointer' is a proposed interpretation rather than a tested mechanism.

anchors.section: Zero-shot limitation and proposed CV/FV roles

key_findings.claim: Methodological exception: two Qwen-2.5-72B categorical datasets were excluded after anomalously large, bimodal causal effects were observed.
key_findings.evidence: French open-ended and multiple-choice categorical CIE values reach a qualitatively different scale and are removed from final AIE calculation. The authors report that the top-five head ranking remains identical, which protects that particular selection result, but no preregistered outlier rule or effect on full-rank AIE, overlap at larger K, and downstream vectors is supplied.

method.core_idea: Separate behavioral mediation from representational invariance by selecting attention heads either through activation patching or through cross-format representational similarity, then compare and intervene with the resulting summed head-output vectors.
method.mechanism: The study builds 1,050 few-shot prompts spanning seven word-level relations and three formats. Mean clean head activations are patched into corrupted prompts to rank heads by average indirect effect; the same heads yield Function Vectors. Independently, head-output cosine matrices are correlated with a same-relation design matrix to select Concept Vector heads. Mean per-format vectors are injected into the residual stream across layers on AmbiguousICL prompts, with target-probability gain, top-1 accuracy, token changes, and ID-to-OOD KL used to compare causal strength and cross-format consistency.
assumptions: Mean-activation patching into shuffled demonstrations localizes the components that normally mediate the relation rather than an artifact of the corruption or intervention.
High RSA against a same-concept design matrix reflects relational abstraction rather than task-specific vocabulary, morphology, or dataset construction artifacts.
Cosine geometry in the ordinary residual metric is meaningful for comparing linear concept representations across heads and formats.
Summing outputs from independently selected heads produces a coherent vector even when the heads occupy different layers.
The AmbiguousICL competition between a first relation and second translation relation is representative of cross-format task control.
Lower post-intervention KL across formats reflects invariance rather than merely weaker perturbations.
Hyperparameters tuned using every format transfer to the reported relations without materially biasing OOD comparisons.
Seven mostly word-level relations in Llama and Qwen capture the abstraction required by broader analogical or compositional reasoning.
A top-K localizer's failure to select a head is evidence of negligible normal causal contribution.

techniques.role: Ranks attention heads by restoration of target-token probability on corrupted ICL prompts.
Ranks heads by same-relation geometry across languages and question formats.
Constructs FVs and CVs from the selected heads' residual-stream outputs.
Creates competing relations so steering must amplify one concept already present in context.
Tests whether extracted vectors causally shift the next-token distribution.
Measures similarity of ID- and OOD-vector intervention distributions.
Checks whether steering carries language or multiple-choice surface tokens.
Tests whether causal-head localization persists when clean and corrupted prompts use different formats.

evaluations.setting: Llama-3.1 8B/70B and Qwen-2.5 7B/72B; seven relations × three formats × 50 prompts
evaluations.metric: Concept RSA, question-type RSA, cosine-similarity structure, and top-K head overlap
evaluations.result: CVs have higher concept and lower format RSA; Llama-70B FV within-format cosine averages 0.90 versus 0.55 for the weaker CV format cluster. Top-5 AIE/RSA overlap is zero in all models.
evaluations.baseline: AIE-selected Function Vectors using the same additive head-output construction.

evaluations.setting: AmbiguousICL steering with 100 prompts per relation and layer sweeps
evaluations.metric: Change in expected-token probability and Top-1 accuracy
evaluations.result: English-extracted FVs generally give the largest ID gains; CVs give smaller gains but more often remain positive across French and multiple-choice extraction. Exact aggregate endpoints and uncertainty are not tabulated.
evaluations.baseline: Unsteered model and corresponding AIE-selected FV intervention.

evaluations.result: English/French/MC CVs raise 'sweet' by 49/54/35 points; the corresponding FVs raise 'sweet' by 56 points ID but favor French subwords or an opening bracket OOD.
evaluations.baseline: Unsteered distribution: French translation at 49% and 'sweet' at 2%.

evaluations.setting: All models, relations, and top five ID-active layers
evaluations.metric: KL divergence from the ID-vector post-steering distribution
evaluations.result: CV KL is lower than FV KL in every displayed model summary, especially for multiple-choice extraction.
evaluations.baseline: FV ID-to-OOD divergence; intervention magnitude is not matched.

evaluations.setting: Zero-shot steering across four models and six non-translation relations
evaluations.result: CV effects are minimal relative to FV effects, indicating that CVs do not reliably instantiate a task absent a contextual demonstration.
evaluations.baseline: FV steering from the same formats and hyperparameter sweep.

evaluations.setting: Llama-3.1-70B cross-format activation patching in all six source-target directions
evaluations.metric: Maximum AIE and top-five overlap with standard FV/CV heads
evaluations.result: FV overlap is 4/2/1/3/4/4 and CV overlap is zero throughout; maximum AIE ranges from 0.01 to 0.41.
evaluations.baseline: Within/all-format standard FV and CV top-five localizers.

evaluations.setting: Spanish relation prompts interleaved with Spanish-to-English translation in Llama-3.1-70B
evaluations.metric: Target-probability steering curves and ID-to-OOD KL
evaluations.result: CVs preserve the same qualitative consistency ordering and English-extracted CVs favor context-appropriate Spanish answers, though both vector types have lower absolute effects than in the main setup.

limitations: Author-stated: the global RSA criterion can miss relation-specific invariant heads.
Author-stated: the study does not examine how FV and CV heads emerge during training or whether and how the two sets interact during inference.
Author-stated negative: CVs have smaller causal effects and are ineffective in zero-shot steering or activation-patching restoration when the relation is absent.
Reviewer-identified: OOD formats participate in steering hyperparameter selection, so reported OOD results are not untouched held-out transfer.
Reviewer-identified: CV selection and the main RSA invariance evaluation reuse the same relation-format prompt collection.
Reviewer-identified: lower CV KL is confounded by the smaller magnitude of CV interventions.
Reviewer-identified: only Llama-3.1 and Qwen-2.5 base-model families, seven word-level relations, and three closely designed formats are tested.
Reviewer-identified: steering curves lack exact aggregate tables, random-seed intervals, bootstrap uncertainty, and statistical comparisons.
Reviewer-identified: cross-format activation patching is only reported for Llama-3.1-70B and has very small effects in some directions.
Reviewer-identified: AmbiguousICL always uses translation as the second competing relation, entangling foreign-language extraction artifacts with the task competition.
Reviewer-identified: categorical and causal pairs are GPT-4o-generated and receive syntactic filtering but no reported human semantic validation or ambiguity audit.
Reviewer-identified: two Qwen-72B datasets are excluded post hoc under no predeclared outlier rule.
Reviewer-identified: the symbolic-pointer interpretation is not supported by a traced content-addressing pathway.
failure_modes: RSA selects heads that encode relation-specific vocabulary or morphology shared across prompts rather than an abstract mapping.
A weak vector appears invariant under KL simply because it barely changes either distribution.
Format-aware tuning overfits French and multiple-choice extraction and fails on a genuinely unseen language, instruction style, or compositional task.
The translation competitor in AmbiguousICL exaggerates foreign-language artifacts and reverses the ranking under a different competing relation.
Mean activation patching creates an off-manifold state that elevates heads useful for recovery but not normally necessary for ICL.
Summing heads from different layers ignores their native computational contexts and produces a vector whose effect is injection-layer dependent.
A relation is absent from the prompt, leaving the CV unable to steer despite strong RSA decodability.
Polysemous, noisy, or culturally specific word pairs make concept clustering reflect dataset artifacts.
Post hoc dataset exclusions or layer/hyperparameter selection change the top-head ranking in another model or relation.
An invariant representation is distributed across MLPs or many weak heads and is missed by the top-K attention-only search.
reusable_insights: Separate causal localization from invariance localization; decodability, organization, and behavioral mediation answer different questions.
Evaluate an invariant vector on formats and concepts not used to select its components or tune its strength.
Magnitude-match interventions before comparing distributional consistency or collateral effects.
Inspect token-level side effects because a successful target-probability change can carry unwanted language or formatting signals.
Include both task-instantiation and task-modulation settings; a representation can steer competition without creating behavior from scratch.
Use multiple competing tasks in ambiguous prompts so OOD artifacts are not aligned with one fixed distractor.
Report full head-score rank correlations and causal ablations in addition to top-K overlap.
Treat absence from an activation-patching top-K as a negative localizer result, not proof that the representation has no causal role.
open_questions: Do CV heads generalize to a language, response schema, and relation family excluded from RSA selection and hyperparameter tuning?
Does the CV-FV KL advantage remain after matching vector norm, ID probability gain, or distributional effect size?
Are CVs necessary under any naturally occurring context, or only sufficient modulators under artificial addition?
What downstream components read CV-head outputs, and is there a causal path from invariant detection to FV execution?
Can relation-specific RSA recover invariant heads missed by the global selector without overfitting?
Do MLPs or distributed subspaces carry stronger invariant representations than the selected attention heads?
How do CV and FV heads develop during pretraining and post-training?
Does the dissociation persist for multi-step analogies, compositional functions, factual relations, and nonverbal formats?
How stable are selected heads across prompt samples, checkpoints, model seeds, and equivalent corruption schemes?
Can causal scrubbing, path patching, or targeted ablation distinguish a pointer/modulator circuit from passive concept decodability?

competitive_landscape.title: Function Vectors in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Todd et al. introduce AIE-selected attention-head Function Vectors and show strong causal transfer across contexts. The present paper reuses that construction, challenges its full format invariance, and adds RSA-selected CVs; the causal FV mechanism itself is prior work.

competitive_landscape.title: In-Context Learning Creates Task Vectors
competitive_landscape.difference: Hendel et al. show that an ICL demonstration set can be compressed into a single task vector that modulates query processing. The present work splits this unitary picture into format-conditioned causal FVs and weaker format-invariant CVs localized at attention-head level.

competitive_landscape.title: Which Attention Heads Matter for In-Context Learning?
competitive_landscape.difference: Yin and Steinhardt compare induction and FV heads across 12 models and use ablations to show FV heads drive few-shot ICL. The present paper accepts that causal role but asks whether a distinct set of heads better preserves relation geometry across format; it uses fewer model families and no necessity ablation of CV heads.

competitive_landscape.title: Do Different Prompting Methods Yield a Common Task Representation in Language Models?
competitive_landscape.difference: Davidson et al. already find that demonstrations and instructions elicit different, partly overlapping causal task representations and heads. The present paper studies open-ended, multilingual, and multiple-choice demonstrations and contributes an explicit RSA-selected invariant alternative rather than only documenting presentation-specific FVs.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Symbolic Mechanisms Support Abstract Reasoning in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. identify symbol-abstraction, symbolic-induction, and retrieval heads that causally support abstract rule induction in Llama-3-70B. Their multi-stage circuit is stronger evidence for symbolic mechanism than CV steering alone; the present work instead isolates format-invariant relational geometry across four models and contrasts it with FV heads.

competitive_landscape.title: Linearity of Relation Decoding in Transformer Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Hernandez et al. show that many relations can be decoded by a linear transformation while documenting important failures of linear encoding. The present work localizes invariant relation information to selected head outputs and tests steering, but its cosine/RSA criterion inherits the limitation that not all relational knowledge is linearly accessible.

competitive_landscape.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. formalize linear representation and argue that meaningful geometry depends on a causal, non-Euclidean inner product. The present paper uses ordinary cosine similarity to infer orthogonality and abstraction, so this prior supplies a direct caveat to its geometric interpretation and a stronger metric control not evaluated here.

competitive_landscape.title: Provable In-Context Vector Arithmetic via Retrieving Task Concepts
competitive_landscape.difference: Bu et al. give a theoretical task-concept retrieval account for vector arithmetic and distributional generalization. The present empirical dissociation argues that one global task vector is incomplete and should be format-conditioned, but it does not test the theorem's training assumptions or supply an alternative formal model.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims that causal Function Vectors are not fully format-invariant, introduces RSA-selected Concept Vectors that encode relational concepts at a higher level of abstraction, shows the two head sets are largely disjoint, and establishes an in-distribution-strength versus out-of-distribution-consistency steering trade-off.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The same head-output construction is compared under causal and representational selectors across 1,050 prompts and four models; top-K overlaps are near zero; token artifacts expose FV format mixing; AmbiguousICL and a Spanish replication show context-sensitive CV steering; zero-shot and cross-format patching provide useful negative results.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The credible novelty is the operational AP-versus-RSA head dissociation and the construction of cross-format RSA-selected vectors with token-level steering controls. Function/task vectors, presentation-specific causal mechanisms, linear relation representations, and symbolic abstraction heads are strong antecedents. Claims of general OOD abstraction should be narrowed because the evaluated formats help tune the intervention, RSA is assessed partly on its selection data, KL is strength-confounded, and the proposed pointer mechanism is not traced. Confidence is high in the descriptive head-overlap and artifact results, and moderate in the broader mechanistic interpretation.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text review covered all 25 pages, including every appendix, prompt construction, overlap significance test, hyperparameter rule, full steering and zero-shot plots, the Qwen outlier exclusion, MC-word control, Spanish AmbiguousICL replication, and six-direction cross-format patching table. The indexed PDF/text pins were checked against the cached files. Eight closest primary arXiv records were checked at their exact current revisions on 2026-08-23. The OOD-tuning issue is a protocol contradiction, while the KL-strength and symbolic-pointer points are explicitly reviewer inferences rather than author admissions.
